{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(
    input [7:0] address,
    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,
    input [7:0] b,
    input control,
    output [15:0] count
);
    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;

    // Preserve the mandatory modulo-256 pointer subtraction.
    wire [7:0] offset1, offset2, offset;
    assign offset1 = base - ptr1;
    assign offset2 = base - ptr2;
    assign offset = control ? offset1 : offset2;

    // Carry-save compression of address + b + (255 - offset).
    wire [7:0] inv_offset, s, c;
    assign inv_offset = ~offset;
    assign s = address ^ b ^ inv_offset;
    assign c = (address & b) | (address & inv_offset)
             | (b & inv_offset);

    // T = address + b + (255 - offset) + 1.
    // Pack the constant one into the vacant low bit of the carry row.
    wire [8:0] x, y;
    assign x = {1'b0, s};
    assign y = {c, 1'b1};

    // Explicit parallel-prefix carry computation for the final addition.
    wire [8:0] p0, g0;
    wire [8:0] p1, g1, p2, g2, p4, g4, p8, g8;
    assign p0 = x ^ y;
    assign g0 = x & y;

    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < 9; i = i + 1) begin : prefix
            if (i >= 1) begin : d1
                assign p1[i] = p0[i] & p0[i-1];
                assign g1[i] = g0[i] | (p0[i] & g0[i-1]);
            end else begin : b1
                assign p1[i] = p0[i];
                assign g1[i] = g0[i];
            end
            if (i >= 2) begin : d2
                assign p2[i] = p1[i] & p1[i-2];
                assign g2[i] = g1[i] | (p1[i] & g1[i-2]);
            end else begin : b2
                assign p2[i] = p1[i];
                assign g2[i] = g1[i];
            end
            if (i >= 4) begin : d4
                assign p4[i] = p2[i] & p2[i-4];
                assign g4[i] = g2[i] | (p2[i] & g2[i-4]);
            end else begin : b4
                assign p4[i] = p2[i];
                assign g4[i] = g2[i];
            end
            if (i >= 8) begin : d8
                assign p8[i] = p4[i] & p4[i-8];
                assign g8[i] = g4[i] | (p4[i] & g4[i-8]);
            end else begin : b8
                assign p8[i] = p4[i];
                assign g8[i] = g4[i];
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    wire [9:0] t;
    assign t[8:0] = p0 ^ {g8[7:0], 1'b0};
    assign t[9] = g8[8];

    // count = T - 256. T ranges from 1 through 766.
    wire negative_result;
    assign negative_result = ~(t[9] | t[8]);
    assign count = {{7{negative_result}}, ~t[8], t[7:0]};
endmodule",

All three supplied critical paths start at control and end at upper count bits, traversing a substantial mapped logic cone rather than only a final selection cell. The final NOR contributes 0.43 ns, and the path also contains relatively slow XOR/XNOR stages. This supports targeting control-dependent arithmetic and upper-result generation. It does not establish a particular serial-adder count: the source-localization evidence identifies only a conservative mux dependency, not exact mapped arithmetic provenance.",
  "rewrite": "Compute both explicitly truncated offsets in parallel, select one 8-bit offset, and compress address, b, and the complemented offset into carry-save rows. A nine-bit parallel-prefix addition, including its carry-out, evaluates T = address + b + (255 - offset) + 1. Generate the upper output byte directly from T instead of expressing a general 16-bit subtract/add result. The exact identity is count = T - 256 modulo 65536.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis, not a measurement: carry-save compression followed by logarithmic carry computation and direct upper-byte decoding may reduce maximum arrival relative to 2.38 ns. The rewrite also makes control select only an 8-bit operand. However, ABC can restructure the prefix network, and selecting an operand before arithmetic can itself become critical. No numerical timing gain or timing eligibility is established without the specified mapping and OpenSTA run.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The candidate shares the result arithmetic and narrows its carry-propagating portion, but the explicit prefix network introduces additional propagate/generate logic and routing fanout. These are opposing area effects; compliance with the 1311.632960 um^2 cap is unmeasured. Accept this candidate only after full equivalence, mapped area at or below the cap, zero max-slew/max-capacitance violations, and a measured maximum data arrival below 2.38 ns under the fixed flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, and parameter declaration/default are preserved. All 33 ordinary input bits remain unconstrained; no state, clocks, assumptions, or don't-cares are introduced. control=1 selects ptr1 and control=0 selects ptr2. Each base-minus-pointer result is explicitly eight bits before further arithmetic. For any eight-bit offset, T lies in [1,766], so T-256 lies in [-255,510]. When T[9:8] is 0, 1, or 2, the required upper byte is respectively FF, 00, or 01, exactly matching the output construction. The algebra also preserves nondefault eight-bit base values, although only the default instance is assessed. Formal equivalence has not been run here."
